title: Mexican authorities raid cartel-linked crypto mining in Puebla, seize 300 GPUs (September 6-8, 2026)
dek: Law enforcement in Puebla, Mexico conducted a raid between September 6-8, 2026, on an illicit crypto mining operation in the Sierra Norte mountains near the Nuevo Necaxa hydroelectric dam. Approximately 300 GPUs, electrical transformers, and satellite antennas were seized. The primary charge is unauthorized electricity siphoning from federal infrastructure, known locally as 'huachicoleo.' Crypto mining itself remains legal in Mexico, but this marks Puebla's fourth such bust since early 2025.
author: Crypto Cronkite
key_fact: Mexican authorities seized approximately 300 GPUs from an illegally powered mining facility near federal hydroelectric infrastructure between September 6-8, 2026, in what marks the fourth such Puebla bust in less than two years.
bottom_line: The fourth Puebla bust in under two years suggests sustained law enforcement focus on cartel-linked mining infrastructure. Whether this represents a growing criminal pivot to energy theft as a money laundering vehicle, or routine enforcement responding to observable operations, depends on comparing electricity theft patterns before and after crypto adoption in the region, data not yet available from the reporting.
body: Mexican authorities conducted a raid on an illicit crypto mining operation in Puebla's Sierra Norte mountains between September 6 and 8, 2026, according to Crypto Briefing's reporting. The facility, located near the Nuevo Necaxa hydroelectric dam, had approximately 300 GPUs, electrical transformers, and satellite antennas seized during the operation.

The primary charge against operators centers on unauthorized siphoning of power from federal hydroelectric infrastructure, a practice locally known as 'huachicoleo.' Crypto mining itself remains legal in Mexico; the violation is the electricity theft. Puebla's security minister Francisco Sánchez noted that the facility's remote location and the noise generated by its operations were key factors that tipped off investigators.

This marks Puebla's fourth bust of an illegal crypto mining operation since early 2025. Authorities suspect organized crime involvement and are investigating potential connections to the Sinaloa Cartel and the Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG), though no direct links to any specific cartel have been validated so far. Investigators have not disclosed which cryptocurrency tokens the facility was mining.

Crypto-related money laundering by Mexican criminal organizations reportedly increased 55.8% in 2025, per Crypto Briefing. Mining crypto with stolen electricity produces coins with no obvious transaction trail back to illicit activity, unlike drug proceeds that require laundering through shell companies or cash-intensive businesses. Mexico's state utility CFE reported electricity theft losses exceeding 6,346 GWh, valued at around 13.8 billion pesos (approximately $817 million), from January through July 2024 alone. That figure covers all forms of electricity theft across the country, not crypto mining specifically.
Investigators have not disclosed what happened to the mined coins, whether any were recovered during or after the raid, or the estimated hash rate or daily production of the seized equipment.
